topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture by framing the session's themes on cellular transformation and outlining the core learning objectives.

topics.label: Viral etiology, oncogene discovery, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the historical study of tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays to evaluate transformed cell phenotypes.

topics.label: Classification and genetic mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the concepts, regulatory pathways, and mutational mechanisms that distinguish oncogenes from tumor suppressor genes.

topics.label: Types, mechanisms, and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate the molecular origins, DNA repair defects, and cellular consequences of chromosomal and sequence instability in cancer.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the stepwise accumulation of mutations during tumor progression and examine how inherited genetic defects accelerate cancer development.

topics.label: Conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer closes the session with concluding remarks, a book recommendation, and framing for the upcoming lecture.
